mechanism_narrative: A low and stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4.5%, it indicates monetary tightening, which can lead to decreased borrowing and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following FEDFUNDS crossing 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) show concurrent growth, it signals a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following concurrent PAYEMS and INDPRO growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts (HOUST) during a late-cycle expansion indicates continued demand strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following HOUST growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity, which is positive for S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following INDPRO growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following RSAFS decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) slows and unemployment (UNRATE) rises concurrently, it indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following concurrent GDPC1 slowdown and UNRATE rise, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary easing cycle reduces borrowing costs, stimulating economic activity and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following FEDFUNDS decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.
